How to read this

Select a thumbnail for frame A. Shift-select or use “Use current as B” for frame B.

Blink steps through dated exposures. Same band selects one detector within a 0.10 µm span. Frames at a similar wavelength make real change easier to judge. Differences are not a detection.

Side by side and Wipe compare two frames. Difference displays A minus B where both frames have usable pixels.

Masked pixels include missing or flagged measurements. Gap fill is for display. Different wavelengths can change brightness.

Keyboard in the image: Space plays or pauses. Left and Right step. Shift + arrow pans. Enter samples a spectrum. Keys 1–4 switch modes. + and − zoom. Home fits.

Data sources, credits and use

SPHEREx data products are from a joint JPL and California Institute of Technology mission funded by NASA and served by NASA/IPAC IRSA. See the SPHEREx acknowledgment ↗ and data citations for DR1 ↗ and QR3 ↗. Challenge-target astrometry is credited to SIMBAD/CDS ↗.

Gaia DR3 data come from ESA, were processed by the Gaia Data Processing and Analysis Consortium, and are provided by MAST/STScI. See the MAST data-use policy ↗.

AllWISE combines WISE (UCLA and JPL/Caltech) and NEOWISE (JPL/Caltech) data, both funded by NASA. Reference positions use the AllWISE catalog ↗ via CDS VizieR ↗. See the AllWISE acknowledgment ↗.

NEOSSat catalog reference: CSA and DRDC, via CADC/NRC. See the NEOSSat acknowledgment and product guide ↗.

Sources, methods & SKYSHIFT

Replay intro →

SKYSHIFT is an independent Project Mercury Team application. It displays dated SPHEREx DR1 and QR3 cutouts with their detector, wavelength and archive source.

Wavelength, processing and masked pixels can change how the same field looks. Treat visual differences as questions to investigate.
